params.body:
Third measurement to carry verdicts, after `deployed` (#170) and `app` (#171).

| facet | thresholds, worst first |
| --- | --- |
| owner (the token Elixir reads with) | `OWNER_TOKEN_REFUSED` (now), `OWNER_TOKEN_EXPIRING_NOW` (<7 days, now), `OWNER_TOKEN_EXPIRING` (<30, week), `OWNER_TOKEN_VALID` (ok) |
| gateway (its copy) | `GATEWAY_TOKEN_REFUSED` (now), `GATEWAY_TOKEN_DIFFERS` (week), `GATEWAY_TOKEN_MISSING` (month), `GATEWAY_TOKEN_SAME` (ok) |
| keys (every key the project acts with) | `CREDENTIAL_REFUSED` (now), `CREDENTIAL_EXPIRING` (<14 days, week), `CREDENTIAL_UNPROVEN` (month), `CREDENTIALS_HONOURED` (ok) |

The 7 and 30 are Portal's card numbers, copied, so no verdict changes. The four `CREDENTIAL_*` entries existed and only gain a level. The scan's two private constants (14 days, 24 hours) move into the registry as well: the per-row state now reads `CREDENTIAL_EXPIRING` and the new `CREDENTIAL_PROOF_STALE`, so no judgement number is left outside `Thresholds`.

Without an answer from GitHub there is no word on the owner or the gateway, only on the keys (the row is unproven, so month), as before.

Tests: eight new cases in `CredentialsScanTest`, one per verdict. Suite 593 green, PHPStan and Pint clean. Portal follows with the card reading `owner`, `gateway` and `keys`.
params.title: Credentials judges its own facts, per party that has to open a door
